inputs.text: More tenancies don’t mean much if people are still being pushed out of their homes. Rising eviction notices, homelessness and emergency accommodation expose a housing system that manages insecurity instead of guaranteeing people a stable place to live. The six-year lease rules introduced on March 1 should be judged by whether they deliver real security—especially for renters most at risk of displacement—not by headline figures that make a deepening crisis look solved. Renter protection must come before appearances.
